original_interpretation: TSMC's FY2025 20-F risk factors warn a major cyberattack could cause loss/divulgence of trade secrets and customers' proprietary information.
evidence_found: "Major cyberattacks could also lead to loss or divulgence of trade secrets and other sensitive information, such as proprietary information of our customers and other stakeholders and personal information of our employees." (FY2025 Form 20-F, Item 3 Key Information - Risk Factors; EDGAR copy filed 2026-04-16)
notes: investor.tsmc.com PDF (SRC-0077) is Cloudflare-gated in the browser; web_extract returned only fragments, so the passage was checked in the identical EDGAR filing (added as new source). Same sentence appears in the FY2023 and FY2024 20-Fs, so this is boilerplate risk language, not a reported incident.

original_interpretation: TSMC-Direct is a system-to-system integration service via third-party software that supports free-format data incl. CAD files and binary data.
evidence_found: "TSMC-Direct℠ is a premium system-to-system integration service between TSMC and its business partners through third-party software." ... The Results: "Free format types such as text, images, CAD files, and binary data" (eFoundry page, TSMC-Direct section)
notes: English-locale page (SRC-0170) extract showed the first sentence only (browser hit Cloudflare); the 'Free format' bullet was read on the Japanese-locale copy (same English text, added as source) and appears in the search snippet for the English URL. Company self-description: reported_claim is correct.

original_interpretation: SEMI P39 (OASIS) is designed mainly to carry hierarchical mask layout between EDA, mask writing and mask inspection/repair tools, and is hardware/software independent.
evidence_found: "This format is designed primarily to encapsulate hierarchical mask layout for interchange between systems such as EDA software, mask writing tools, and mask inspection/repair tools. This format is designed to be both hardware- and software-independent." (SEMI store, P39 abstract; current revision P39-0416)

original_interpretation: OASIS was defined by a working group formed by SEMI's Data Path Task Force in autumn 2001, drawing on International SEMATECH mask-EDA meetings.
evidence_found: "In the fall of 2001, SEMI's Data Path Task Force formed a working group to define a successor to the venerable GDSII Stream format"; "In the months leading up to the formation of the SEMI Data Path Task Force, International SEMATECH sponsored a series of meetings focusing on Mask EDA issues. Many of the Task Force participants were also involved..." (P39 abstract, Background)
notes: Minor nuance: the SEMATECH meetings preceded the Task Force's formation and informed it via overlapping participants.

original_interpretation: Photronics says the photomasks it makes incorporate circuit designs customers provide on a confidential basis.
evidence_found: "The photomasks we manufacture incorporate circuit designs provided to us on a confidential basis by our customers." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1 Business - Industry)

original_interpretation: Photronics' mask workflow: receive/convert design data, expose blank, develop/etch, inspect vs design data, repair, clean, pellicle, final inspection, ship.
evidence_found: "The typical manufacturing process for a photomask involves the receipt and conversion of circuit design data to manufacturing pattern data. A lithography system then exposes the circuit pattern onto a photomask blank. The exposed areas are developed and etched ... inspected for defects and conformity to the customer's design data. After the repair of any defects, the photomask is cleaned, any required pellicles ... are applied" (10-K Item 1)
notes: Source calls this the 'typical' process.

original_interpretation: Photronics must pass a qualification/correlation process with each customer before becoming approved supplier; often then gets a specified share of that customer's mask orders while competitive.
evidence_found: "Generally, Photronics and each of its customers engage in a qualification and correlation process before we become an approved supplier. ... In many instances, we enter into sales arrangements with an understanding that, as long as our performance is competitive, we will receive a specified percentage of that customer's photomask orders." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1, p. 5-6)
notes: Source hedges with 'Generally' and 'In many instances'; claim's 'often' is faithful.

original_interpretation: Photronics: order-to-shipment typically 1 day to 3 weeks for a significant part of revenue; some IC mask backlog up to 2-3 months.
evidence_found: "Because of the short period between order and shipment dates (typically from one day to three weeks) for a significant amount of our revenue ... However, the demand for some IC photomasks can extend beyond the traditional time period; thus, for some products, our backlog can expand to as long as two to three months." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1)
notes: Same passage also says the first several layers are sometimes due within 24 hours of receiving design data.

original_interpretation: Photronics says most of its customers use more than one photomask supplier.
evidence_found: "The photomask industry is highly competitive, and most of our customers utilize more than one photomask supplier." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1A Risk Factors); also Item 1 Competition: "most of our customers utilize multiple photomask suppliers."

original_interpretation: Photronics sold to ~636 customers in FY2025 (ended Oct 2025); top five customers ~50% of revenue.
evidence_found: "During 2025, we sold our products to approximately 636 customers." ... "Our five largest customers, in the aggregate, accounted for approximately 50%, 50% and 51% of our revenue in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1; fiscal year ended October 31, 2025)
notes: Latest available: FY2026 10-K not due until ~Dec 2026. Same section: Customers A/B/C = 16%/13%/8% of FY2025 revenue; two largest = 29%.

original_interpretation: SEMI P44 defines OASIS.MASK, an OASIS-based common mask data format applying to mask-tool input data.
evidence_found: "This Standard defines the common mask data format specifications based on OASIS for mask tools, namely 'OASIS.MASK'. OASIS.MASK specification applies to the input data format for mask tools." (SEMI store, P44 abstract)

original_interpretation: SEMI P44 first published Nov 2005 (P44-1105); current P44-1216, reapproved Jan 2024.
evidence_found: "SEMI P44-1216 (Reapproved 0124) - Current"; "Revision History SEMI P44-1216 (Reapproved 0124) SEMI P44-1216 (technical revision) SEMI P44-0316 ... SEMI P44-1105 (first published)" (SEMI store, P44 page). SEMI Standards Watch: Primary Standard "shall be given the (Reapproved mmyy) designation".
notes: The month reading relies on SEMI's mmyy publication date code, confirmed by SEMI's Procedure Manual note (added source).

original_interpretation: SEMI P45 defines MALY, a common job deck format for mask tools, referencing P39 and P44.
evidence_found: "This Document defines the common job deck data format specifications for mask tools, namely 'MALY'. MALY specification applies to the input data format for mask tools. Referenced SEMI Standards ... SEMI P39 ... SEMI P44" (SEMI store, P45 abstract; current P45-0421, first published P45-0306)

original_interpretation: SEMI P10 standardises photomask-order data structures for automated order placement and automated return of mask results/qualification data.
evidence_found: "intended to facilitate the transmittal of mask order data between software systems to allow: automated order placement by mask customers and ... automatic processing of such orders by mask shops, and automated delivery of actual mask results and qualification data by mask shops and ... automatic processing of such data by mask customers." (P10 abstract)

original_interpretation: Latest SEMI P10 revision P10-1112 is Inactive (conditions for Current not met) but SEMI says inactive standards remain valid.
evidence_found: "Revision: SEMI P10-1112 - Inactive"; "NOTICE: This Standard or Safety Guideline has an Inactive Status because the conditions to maintain Current Status have not been met. Inactive Standards or Safety Guidelines are available from SEMI and continue to be valid for use." (SEMI store, P10 page)

original_interpretation: SEMI P10 defines only the transmitted file format (UTF-8, authorised XML implementation), not a database or programming language.
evidence_found: "This structure only defines the data format for the transmitted file. No particular database or programming language is specified by this Standard, except that an authorized implementation in Extensible Markup Language (XML) format will be posted on the SEMI P10 Web site ... The data file is to be transmitted as a UTF-8 file." (P10 abstract)
notes: Abstract adds that it is compatible with SECS-II.

original_interpretation: Samsung SAFE integrates certified PDKs, design methodologies and IP plus cloud, design services, MDI and OSAT 2.5D/3D packaging support.
evidence_found: "SAFE™ accelerates development ... by integrating a range of certified key design components that include process design kits (PDKs), design methodologies (DMs), and intellectual properties (IPs). Additionally, the program provides advanced support with cloud-based integration, design methodology documents and scripts, design services, multi-die integration (MDI), and OSAT advanced 2.5D and 3D packaging." (SAFE page, intro)
notes: Company self-description; reported_claim correct.

original_interpretation: Samsung SAFE IP partner flow: NDA/process plans/PDK+MPW reservation; development support, MPW shuttle, silicon characterisation review; register on CONNECT once QCP standards met.
evidence_found: "Signing of Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) Sharing process development plans Providing PDKs/DKs and MPW shuttle reservation services"; "Conducting MPW shuttle and providing sample chips Managing processes — such as silicon characterization result review"; "Once an IP completes development and meets the SAFE™ QCP's performance and quality standards, partners can register it on CONNECT™" (SAFE IP page, flow chart steps 1-3)
notes: Read in browser (rendered text). The 'As of July 31, 2025 this page is no longer available' string in the raw extract belongs to a contact-form modal, not this page.

original_interpretation: Samsung certifies EDA tools/reference flows via SAFE-QEDA and supplies RTL-to-GDS 'Foundry DM' documents and scripts.
evidence_found: "Samsung Foundry offers a wide range of RTL-GDS¹ conversion-design-methodology documents and scripts (also known as 'Foundry DM')"; "the Electronic Design Automation (EDA) reference flows provided through the tool chain of EDA partners are certified through the SAFE-QEDA program"; "SAFE-QEDA, an accurate and in-depth EDA tool certification program" (SAFE EDA page)

original_interpretation: Samsung SAFE EDA partner list names 18 companies incl. Cadence, Siemens, Synopsys, Empyrean, Primarius, Semitronix, ASML, KLA.
evidence_found: 'Meet Our SAFE™ EDA Partners' logo alt texts (18): Arcas, Arteris, ASML, Cadence, Empyrean, Shenzhen Hongxin Micro-Nano Technology Co., Ltd., IC Manage, IROC Technologies, Keysight, KLA, Lorentz Solution, Phlexing, Primarius, Real Intent, Semitronix, Siemens, Synopsys, Xpeedic (SAFE EDA page, read 2026-10-01)
notes: Counted 18 logos myself from image alt attributes; page carries no as-of date. A partner list on a company page is better typed reported_claim than fact (code caps reported_claim at medium).

original_interpretation: TSMC says EDA Alliance partners' tools cover all IC design stages from timing analysis/simulation through P&R, physical verification and RC extraction for signoff.
evidence_found: "EDA partners in TSMC EDA Alliance offer wide variety of design automation tools that cover all stages of IC design needs, ranging from circuit design timing analysis, simulation for design electrical analysis, place & route for physical implementation, and physical layout verification, RC extraction for final design tapeout signoff." (EDA Alliance page)

original_interpretation: TSMC says selected EDA partners co-develop roadmap-aligned tool features and Reference Flows with its design technology teams and access TSMC insights to validate tools.
evidence_found: "Selected EDA Alliance partners work closely with TSMC's design technology teams to address customer design needs through the enablement of new EDA tool features that align with TSMC advanced process development roadmap, as well as the implementation of TSMC's design methodology in Reference Flows. ... EDA Alliance partners gain access to TSMC's technical insights to validate their tools and methodologies." (EDA Alliance page)

original_interpretation: TSMC EDA Alliance listed 11 partners as of 2026-09-23 (Cadence, iROC, Jedat, Keysight, Lorentz, Primarius, Siemens EDA, Silvaco, SkillCAD, Synopsys, Zuken).
evidence_found: "List of EDA Alliance partners as of 09/23/2026 - Cadence Design Systems - iROC Technologies - Jedat - Keysight Technologies - Lorentz Solution - Primarius - Siemens EDA - Silvaco - SkillCAD - Synopsys - Zuken" (EDA Alliance page)
notes: Count of 11 confirmed. For context, TSMC's Oct 2021 blog cited 16 EDA partners and its 2020 annual report 18, so the list has shrunk. Company list: reported_claim would be the stricter type.

original_interpretation: TSMC9000 sets minimum IP quality requirements; partners submit data, TSMC assesses/scores IP (pre-silicon physical review, post-silicon assessment) and posts scores, known-issue labels and production records on TSMC-Online.
evidence_found: "defines a set of minimum IP quality requirements. IP partners submit data and apply ... Assessment results are posted on TSMC-Online"; "physical review and pre-silicon assessment ... before test chip tape-outs ... followed by typical and split lot silicon assessments"; "TSMC9000 also labels the IP(s) which had been identified with known issues"; "TSMC9000 scores, production records and labels" (IP Alliance page)
notes: The pre-/post-silicon steps are stated for hardened IP; a TSMC9000A automotive extension adds further assessments.

original_interpretation: TSMC does not guarantee silicon-verified third-party IP will work in a design or reach a yield; each catalogue IP is sold and supported directly by the partner.
evidence_found: "All IPs in the TSMC IP catalog are created, directly sold and directly supported by the individual IP partner"; "Note: TSMC does not guarantee that silicon-verified IP will work in any given design environments or achieve certain production yield ratios. In addition, TSMC is not responsible for commitments made to customers by ecosystem partners." (IP Alliance page)

original_interpretation: As of Aug 2023, 60,000+ IPs from IP alliance members supported hundreds of TSMC processes; IP Alliance page cites 40 members.
evidence_found: "As of August 2023, there are a total 60,000+ IPs with dozens of IP types from ecosystem IP alliance members supporting hundreds of TSMC process technologies"; "The TSMC IP catalog contains over tens of thousands of IP options from 40 IP alliance members." (IP Alliance page). Newer: "Accumulated around 93,000 items in broad range of IP portfolio" (TSMC 2025 Sustainability Report, p. 48)
correction: Correctly quoted, but the August 2023 60,000+ IP figure is superseded: TSMC's 2025 Sustainability Report says the IP Alliance had accumulated around 93,000 IP portfolio items by 2025, adding one new member that year (new claim, supersedes CLM-1475). The 40-member count on the page still stands.
notes: Both quotes are on the current page and the 40-member count is current, but the IP count is a stale August 2023 figure.

original_interpretation: TSMC's IP Tag Specification (an enhancement of VSIA's) tracks IP in customers' tape-out databases and feeds published IP volume-production usage records.
evidence_found: "The purpose of TSMC9000 IP Tag Specification, an enhancement of VSIA's IP Tag Specification, is to offer better IP tracking records and provide information from customers' tape-out database. The IP tracking record is used for IP usage analysis ... The volume production record of IP usage summary is posted on TSMC-Online" (IP Alliance page)
notes: 'Embeds tags' is a fair reading of 'enabling tagging of your IP(s)'. The page adds that TSMC gives open access to the spec.

original_interpretation: TSMC IP Alliance members can access TSMC technical data/libraries and get dedicated account managers and technical support.
evidence_found: "IP Alliance members can access TSMC technical data and/or libraries to design their IP, are assigned dedicated account managers and get dedicated support from TSMC IP technical support teams." (IP Alliance page)

original_interpretation: TSMC certifies the security of cloud design environments; Cloud Alliance members: AWS, Cadence, Google Cloud, IC-Link by imec, Microsoft Azure, Siemens, Synopsys.
evidence_found: "Cloud security certified by TSMC ensures data protection for customers to conduct IC design securely in the Cloud." Member logos: Amazon Web Services, Cadence, Google Cloud, IC-Link by imec, Microsoft Azure, Siemens, Synopsys (Cloud Alliance page)
notes: 7 members, matching the claim. 'With its collateral' comes from the 2018 PR (SRC-0494), not this page. The IC-Link logo path is dated 2026-04, so that member was likely added recently.

original_interpretation: TSMC announced OIP Cloud Alliance (5th alliance after EDA, IP, DCA, VCA) in Oct 2018 with AWS, Cadence, Azure, Synopsys certifying RTL-to-GDSII and custom flows in the cloud.
evidence_found: "Oct 3, 2018 – TSMC ... announced the 5th Open Innovation Platform®, the OIP Cloud Alliance ... The inaugural members, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Cadence, Microsoft Azure, and Synopsys, have worked with TSMC to certify ... both Digital RTL to GDSII and Custom schematic capture ... flows in the Cloud."; "5 Alliances: the EDA Alliance, IP Alliance, Design Center Alliance, Value Chain Aggregator Alliance, and the newest, the Cloud Alliance."
notes: Historical (2018). OIP has since added a sixth alliance (3DFabric, 2022), per TSMC's 2025 Sustainability Report.

original_interpretation: Synopsys said in 2018 its cloud solution passed TSMC security and performance audits for designing in the cloud with TSMC collateral.
evidence_found: "The Synopsys Cloud Solution has passed the rigorous TSMC security and performance audits and is ready for our mutual customers to design in the cloud with TSMC collateral using Synopsys tools and IP." (Synopsys quote, Deirdre Hanford, in TSMC PR of 3 Oct 2018)
notes: Third-party quote inside a TSMC release; reported_claim is correct.

original_interpretation: TSMC launched OIP in 2008 (45nm leading edge), giving partners/customers early access to TSMC technology so EDA/IP could be ready at process launch.
evidence_found: "launching the TSMC Open Innovation Platform® (OIP) in 2008, when 45nm was cutting edge ... Access to TSMC technology during early development phases was made possible to enable parallel development with partners and customers."; "synchronization of EDA and IP availability with the introduction of TSMC's most advanced processes" (TSMC blog, 25 Oct 2021)
notes: The 2008 launch year is also stated in TSMC's 2025 Sustainability Report.

original_interpretation: TSMC says OIP synchronises EDA flows and IP design kits with DRM and SPICE model releases for new processes.
evidence_found: "This enables customer adoption of TSMC's newest processes with EDA flows that have been enabled and pipe-cleaned, and IP design kits made available in synchrony with DRMs and Spice models." (TSMC blog, 25 Oct 2021)

original_interpretation: In Oct 2021 TSMC said it provided 2,600+ PDKs, 38,000+ technology files and 40,000+ IP titles spanning 0.5um-3nm.
evidence_found: "Expanding its libraries and silicon IP portfolio to more than 40,000 IP titles and providing more than 38,000 technology files as well as over 2,600 process design kits spanning 0.5-micron to 3-nanometer to customers" (TSMC blog, 25 Oct 2021). Newer: "Cumulatively released over 3,900 PDK (Process Design Kit), 58,000 technology files, and 77 design reference flows"; IP Alliance "around 93,000 items" (2025 Sustainability Report, p. 48)
correction: Accurate for Oct 2021, but superseded: TSMC's 2025 Sustainability Report gives over 3,900 PDKs, 58,000 technology files and 77 design reference flows released cumulatively, and around 93,000 IP portfolio items (new claims supersede CLM-1472 and CLM-1475).
notes: Counting basis may differ ('providing' vs 'cumulatively released'), so use the series as a trend, not exact growth.
